newsitem.title: USA: Tandy posts loses for quarter, year after big charges.
newsitem.headline: Tandy posts loses for quarter, year after big charges.

text.p: Tandy Corp. said Thursday that it posted big losses for the fourth quarter and all of 1996 after taking charges for restructuring and accounting changes.
"Calendar 1996 represented a very difficult year for the entire consumer electronics industry and a major re-engineering year for Tandy," the company said in a statement.

Tandy, one of the nation's biggest retailers of consumer electronics best known for its Radio Shack stores, said it lost $137.7 million, or $2.39 a share, in the three months ended Dec. 31, when it took pre-tax charges of $136.6 million for restructuring and $86.8 million to account for the impairment of long-lived assets.
That compared with a profit of $90.2 million, or $1.39 a share, in the same period in 1995.

Tandy, which said in December that it would close its 19 Computer City stores and sell its Incredible Universe "superstores," said its sales in the fourth quarter, which includes the important holiday shopping season, slipped to $2.05 billion from $2.09 billion.
For all of 1996 Tandy said it lost $91.6 million, or $1.64 a share, after taking charges of $162.1 million for restructuring and $112.8 million for asset impairment.
The company, which is based in Fort Worth, Texas, had net income of $211.97 million, or $3.12 a share, for all of 1995.
Tandy said its revenues for all of last year expanded to $6.29 billion from $5.84 billion.
Tandy's stock added $1 to $48 in afternoon trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
